To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the communicative language teaching (CLT) approach has been widely implemented in the past two decades in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond; (2) the CLT approach is not a single, monolithic approach, but a set of approaches with a variety of theoretical and pedagogical assumptions, which are implemented in different ways in different contexts; (3) the implementation of CLT has not been successful in all cases; (4) the implementation of the CLT approach has
CLT is a complex, multifaceted approach, which can be implemented in different ways, depending on the educational context and the teacher’s professional background and training.
the use of a CLT approach to language teaching is a complex process and that there is no single best way to teach languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the main characteristics of CLT?
the nature of the communicative language teaching approach and how it can be adapted to suit the needs of different groups of learners in different contexts.
how language teaching and language learning can be understood in terms of the communicative processes that are central to the human condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have not arrived at the end, but we are now at a stage where we can begin to see the end.
we are now at a point where we have to start all over again, but with a much more solid foundation than we had in the 1970s and 1980s.
CLT is not a method but a philosophy of language teaching, and that it has become the dominant philosophy of language teaching in the 21st century.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we need to continue to refine our understanding of communicative competence, develop our understanding of how language and communication can be taught and learnt, and explore how we can best integrate the insights of CLT with the insights of other approaches.
CLT is a process, not a product.
CLT is a useful concept for the 21st Century but one which needs to be constantly reinterpreted to take account of changing contexts and new insights.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CLT is a complex construct that needs to be unpacked and reassembled to suit the needs of specific contexts.
CLT is still a useful concept in language teaching, but it is not a single approach.
CLT is still very much alive and well in Asia and elsewhere.
